passages.original: hic certe, sicut scriptum est, filius malus ipse se iustum dicit, exitum autem suum non abluit, hoc est non excusat, non diluit, non defendit, quod furore schismatico in haereticam pestem de domo dei exire non timuit, quia, si uere iustus esset, sicut apostolus Paulus cum fratribus falsis, de quibus in suis epistulis ingemit, et sicut Cyprianus cum eis, quos sine baptismo suis peccatis praeteritis plenos existimabat et admitti ad ec. clesiam ab Stephano sciebat, ita in ecclesia Christi cum eis, quos iniustos uel nouerat uel putabat, sine ulla sui commaculatione persisteret nec bonos propter malos desereret, sed malos propter bonos potius toleraret, tamquam granum cum palea pondere caritatis trituram ferens, non tamquam leuissimus puluis etiam ante uentilationem flatibus cedens.
passages.english: Here certainly, as it is written, the wicked son calls himself righteous, but does not wash away his going out, that is, he does not excuse it, does not wash it out, does not defend it, namely that in schismatic fury he did not fear to go out from the house of God into the plague of heresy. For if he were truly righteous, then, just as the apostle Paul [remained] with the false brethren over whom he groans in his letters, and just as Cyprian [remained] with those whom he judged to be without baptism and full of their past sins, and whom he knew to be admitted to the Church by Stephen, so he would persist in the Church of Christ, without any defilement of himself, with those whom he either knew or supposed to be unrighteous. He would not desert the good because of the bad, but would rather tolerate the bad for the sake of the good, bearing the threshing like grain with the chaff, by the weight of charity, and not yielding to the winds, like the lightest dust, even before the winnowing.
passages.notes: 'filius malus ipse se iustum dicit, exitum autem suum non abluit' alludes to Proverbs 24 (Old Latin/Septuagint form), which Augustine then glosses. 'ec. clesiam' read as 'ecclesiam' (scanning error). Stephen is Pope Stephen I, Cyprian's opponent in the rebaptism controversy.
